reason: The draft answers Marisol's question directly: she shouldn't keep running this volume. It also explains why in a useful way: heart and lungs adapt in days, but calves and tendons take weeks. Next week adds up to 40 mi (6+8+7+5+14). That makes sense after 37 mi, and the 53 mi week isn't treated as the new baseline. Cutting the long run to 14 mi is cautious. The plan keeps her five-day pattern, with rest on Monday and Friday, the session on Wednesday and the long run on Sunday. Heart-rate caps and paces make every day runnable as written, and threshold reps at 8:00/mi fit a 3:45 goal. The plan flags the calf tightness and seems to include stop cues. But it keeps the Wednesday threshold session without saying clearly that it depends on the calves feeling fine. Tightness that eases is not pain, so this isn't unsafe, but the plan should have made that condition explicit. Points off for details the card doesn't support: a '20-miler', 'HR 139' and 'your usual hip and glute work' are stated as facts. They may be true, but the card doesn't show them.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 32, 24, 27, 37 mi
This week: 53 mi over 6 runs. Planned 38 mi, ran 53 mi.
Body: "Calves tight on Sunday night, otherwise great."
Feeling: "Like I've turned a corner."
Asks: "I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: The 20-miler shows your fitness is there, but 53 miles against a planned 38 is too big a jump to repeat. …
Answers: (1) Not at this volume, so the plan takes you back to about 40 miles this week. You felt fine because your heart and lungs adapt in days, while calves, tendons and joints take weeks. (2) Keep the way you ran: easy days at heart rate 139, steady threshold reps and an even long run. Add distance in steps of about 10 percent, with a lighter week every third or fourth week.
Safety flag: Calf tightness after the 20 miler
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full rest after the 20 miler, with no short run even if you feel good, so…
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145 and pace around 9:50 to 10:00/mi, flat route. Stop…
Wed: quality, 8 mi, 2 mi easy warm-up, then 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi with 3 min easy jog…
Thu: easy, 7 mi, heart rate under 145 and pace around 9:50 to 10:00/mi. Flushes out…
Fri: rest. Your usual hip and glute work is fine, but no running; rest days are where…
Sat: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, optionally finishing with 4 x 20 s relaxed…
Sun: long, 14 mi, heart rate under 145 and pace 10:00 to 10:20/mi. Agree the 14 mi with…
